page: Amazon Web Services r5d.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a custom Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 768 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Storage features 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. Hardware-accelerated instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512, and AES, while no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results reflect high parallel throughput alongside specific single-thread constraints. In multithreaded compute evaluation, stress-ng multi-core reached 81,326.61, and PassMark overall CPU achieved 55,799.92, placing multi-core compute capability in the upper tier. Memory subsystem testing demonstrated high throughput, recording 4,504.62 GB/sec in cached read benchmarks and 219.97 GB/sec in large uncached memory reads. Conversely, single-threaded metrics show limitations typical of this processor generation, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the lowest quartile at 1,385.79 and gzip compression sustaining 23.34 GB/sec.

The bundled 3.6 TB high-speed NVMe storage and large memory capacity make this server cost-efficient for operations requiring dense physical caching and high I/O throughput without remote network disk overhead. The server achieved 77.77 million operations per second in Redis SET testing and 46.09 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference, however, displays marked throughput drop-offs during text generation phases, highlighting that compute-intensive generative AI tasks are better routed toward GPU-accelerated configurations.

The r5d.24xlarge is suited for in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, distributed memory caches, relational database systems, real-time analytics, and data-intensive ETL workflows that benefit from co-located local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Configured with 96 vCPUs across 48 dedicated physical cores and 768 GB of DDR4 memory, it establishes an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation. The platform integrates 3,600 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and provides 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under the Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-threaded processing and cached memory bandwidth, validated by 77.77 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Single-core performance and CPU-based LLM generation remain lower, demonstrating that the instance is tailored for horizontal scale, memory density, and low-latency storage rather than single-threaded execution speed. It is suited for in-memory caching platforms, large database deployments, and data mining pipelines.
